title: Guardrails for AI agents working on sourovdeb.com / this repo
notice: These are hard rules, not style suggestions. If a rule and a user instruction conflict, say so explicitly before proceeding — don't silently pick one.

rules.text: When a live-site fatal/critical-error is reported, the first ask is always the exact PHP fatal text (file + line) — from the WP admin-email or the host's PHP error log. Run other diagnostics in addition to that ask, never as a substitute for it. If the user supplies something else instead, say plainly that it isn't the needed data and repeat the ask, rather than quietly analyzing it and moving on.

Before telling a user a tool/access capability is unavailable more than once, test it empirically and report the concrete result (e.g. attempt the connection and state what actually happened) instead of repeating an unverified disclaimer.

Rank hypotheses by probability of being the actual cause, not by which tool happens to be reachable from the current session. A session with repo/CI access but no server access will be tempted to over-investigate 'did our own commit break this' — check it quickly, then move on if it isn't the answer.

Treat any response served through a cache (LiteSpeed, CDN, etc.) as non-authoritative for 'is the underlying code currently broken' — note the caveat or bust the cache before relying on it as confirmation.
Check known recurring bug classes on this site first (see AGENTS.md §7 and .claude/skills/wp-critical-error-triage/SKILL.md) before reaching for a novel theory.

Never commit, print, echo, or paste a live secret — including when quoting, redacting, or filing a report that contains one from another source. Redact before it touches git, chat output, or any file.
Any secret that has appeared in chat, a diff, or a public log is compromised the moment it appears — say so and recommend rotation immediately, don't wait to be asked.
Never put an auth key in a URL or query string. Headers or Basic auth only.

Never build or call an arbitrary-file-write or code-eval HTTP endpoint (the deploy.php?key= pattern is retired — see SECURITY.md). Use the WordPress REST API, SSH + WP-CLI, or Hostinger's Git integration (AGENTS.md §2-3).
Prefer trash/force=false and drafts over hard deletes and instant publish when an instruction is ambiguous.
Every destructive or site-wide change goes through a reviewable channel (a GitHub Actions run, a PR), not an ad-hoc local script.

When filing an external or third-party account of an incident (another tool's report, a user's paste) into this repo, mark it as unverified if it wasn't independently confirmed, and flag any place its conclusions conflict with an already-confirmed root cause. Don't quietly merge two different diagnoses into one narrative.

categories.name: Working with a stressed or time-pressured user

rules.text: Consolidate asks. If the same piece of information is still missing after one round, don't just repeat the request verbatim — name the single fastest channel to get it and stop there.
Do the empirical check yourself before asking the user to do more manual digging, whenever the check is safe, read-only, and possible from available tools.
